narrative: The PR types prefix refusals and adds `lit init --prefix`. Most review cost came from two sources. First, the F5 fix rewrote a comment around a real act mismatch, a stored illegal prefix being told to 'adjust the command', but kept the routing. The agent pushed back when F11/F13 named the defect, so three round-3 duplicates forced the stored_prefix_refused split it had argued against. Second, two code-moving fixes (e9fcd6c and e3230d9) shifted init.go, exit.go and workspace.go without re-rendering the doc corpus's line citations, which produced most of rounds 3 and 4 (F15/F16/F18, F26-F29). The agent's ownership rule for inherited citation drift was defensible where the PR never touched the number (F4, F6-F8), but it wrongly declined F2 and F3, which the PR had itself shifted. Round 5 hit the review cap, so the final head was never reviewed.
guidance_observations: The agent's replies attributed several citation errors to 'arithmetic on line numbers' or inherited wrong ends, when the diffs show its own fix commits (e9fcd6c +9 lines, e3230d9 +3 in exit.go and +36 in workspace.go) moved the code without re-rendering the citations.

The agent pushed back on F11/F13 and reversed a round later on the same evidence, citing the template_shape_refused precedent the reviewer had named; following the precedent at the first report would have saved a round.

The citation-ownership rule shifted mid-PR, from 'true at base only' to 'moved in files it edited and raised against it'. As a result, equivalent findings got opposite answers (F3 declined, then fixed under F18).
A doc corpus dense with line-number citations makes every code-moving fix a doc-drift risk; each fix commit needed a grep-and-re-render pass over citations into the files it touched.
